page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; small marginal marks and references in the right margin; bottom right, faint fragments below the text block; signature "B 4" at bottom left.

main_text.p: eos voluit, qui annuos magistratus omnis generis gererent, & reipublicæ curandæ administrandæque potestatem haberent. Reliquæ plebi, quæ quarta classe censebatur, & numero priores omnes multum superabat, quam cxsτῶν θητῶν[?], id est, operariorum aut mercenariorum vocabant, judicia & obeundarum concionum jus, communia huic cum cæteris futura, assignavit. Quod, ut Plutarchus ait, initio pene nihil visum, post usu ipso ingens omnino deprehensum. Plurimæ enim controversiæ ad judicia illa deferebantur, & quæcunque earum ad cognitionem magistratuum pertinebant, de iis omnibus provocare ad judicia cuilibet volenti li-[?]cebat. Penes concionem autem rerum summa, & mandandorum honorum, qui per suffragia conferebantur, potestas erat. Et Aristoteles libro politicorum secundo, capite decimo, qui locus x2apud eum illustris est, scribit, existimare quosdam, pene nimium à Solone plebi esse indultum, qui & judiciorum constituendorum, & eligendorum magistratuum, rationumque ab ipsis reposcendarum potestatem ei concesserit. page.notes: Printed page number "23" at top right. Running head as printed. Greek word after "quam" is partly obscured by a superscript and marked [?]. The hyphenated word "li-cebat" at the line end is partly covered by a margin mark; the reading "li-" is doubtful. Right-margin marks "cxs", "x2" and similar small marks are damaged and only partly legible; those shown are the most likely readings. Faint fragments at the bottom right ("stra. oIo." and "iggi") are cut off and appear to belong to the neighbouring page or show-through, so they are not transcribed. The last line ends in a hyphen ("magi-") and continues on the next page.
